missing_details: Definition of the group ring K[G]
Assumption that K is a field
Assumption that G is a torsion-free group
refined_question: Let K be a field and G a torsion-free group. Does the group ring K[G] simultaneously satisfy all of the following three properties: 1. It has no nontrivial zero divisors (i.e. if x,y∈K[G] satisfy xy=0 then x=0 or y=0)? 2. It has no nontrivial idempotents (i.e. if e∈K[G] satisfies e^2=e then e=0 or e=1)? 3. It has no nontrivial units (i.e. if u,v∈K[G] satisfy uv=1 then u=kg and v=(k^{-1}g^{-1}) for some nonzero scalar k∈K and group element g∈G)?
justification: The name “Kaplansky's conjectures” indicates only that Irving Kaplansky proposed multiple conjectures, but does not specify that they concern the structure of group rings K[G] under the assumptions K is a field and G is torsion-free, nor does it define what “nontrivial” zero divisors, idempotents, or units are. The canonical formulation consists of three precise statements about K[G], each requiring those domain and definitional details to be fully understood.
